synopsis: SAE appears as a source for autonomous-tractor training data, off-road digital twins, and on-road AEB validation; its reported 50 million images conflicts with Vision Systems Design's 200 million image pairs for Deere obstacle detection [f821]. A 2026 SAE paper describes a Unity-based multimodal off-road digital twin with procedural terrain, cameras, lidar, GPS, IMU, dynamic weather and lighting, and failure annotations [f3790, f4165]. The booklet includes this simulator alongside MAVS and other examples in its assessment that procedural site generation has a strong off-road record [f3734, f4194]. In a separate SAE paper dated 27 September 2016, Salaani and colleagues used an instrumented Volvo tractor-trailer with Bendix radar and AEB for hardware-in-the-loop simulation, benchmarking physical track tests before comparing equivalent simulated scenarios [f10603, f10604]. That validation example is explicitly on-road, so the supplied facts do not establish equivalent validation results for heavy off-road machines [f10603, f10604].
